speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin evaluating your headache and worsening vision, could you please describe the specific nature of the pain and which eye or eyes are affected?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given your age and the combination of headache and visual changes, I need to assess for temporal arteritis. Have you experienced any jaw pain when chewing, scalp tenderness, or new muscle aches, particularly in your shoulders and hips?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned no other pain, but let me confirm: do you have any jaw claudication or scalp tenderness? I also need to check your blood pressure and examine your temporal arteries for tenderness or thickening.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient has hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She also has a history of high cholesterol. Social history: Retired school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing your medical history. I will now examine your temporal arteries for tenderness or thickening and check your blood pressure. Do you experience any pain or discomfort when I gently palpate the area around your temples?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. No recent travel or sick contacts. No changes in hearing. Denies neck stiffness or photophobia.

speaker: Doctor
text: I am noting your denial of nausea, vomiting, and neck stiffness, which helps rule out some other causes. Since we still need to confirm the diagnosis and assess the severity of inflammation, REQUEST TEST: ESR and CRP levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal inflammatory markers make giant cell arteritis less likely. Let me examine your optic discs and check for papilledema, and I will also request a brain MRI to rule out other causes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal inflammatory markers and lack of systemic symptoms make giant cell arteritis unlikely. I need to evaluate for intracranial pathology, so REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRI rules out a tumor or stroke, so I need to examine your optic discs directly. I will now perform a fundoscopy to check for papilledema or other signs of optic nerve pathology.

speaker: Doctor

Fundoscopy reveals bilateral papilledema, which strongly suggests increased intracranial pressure despite the normal MRI. I will now request a lumbar puncture to measure the opening pressure and analyze the cerebrospinal fluid.
REQUEST TEST: Lumbar Puncture

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the patient's age, headache, visual changes, bilateral papilledema, and normal MRI/CSF composition, this presentation is most consistent with idiopathic intracranial hypertension, though atypical for her demographic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension
